previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for elective right total knee arthroplasty but developed postoperative complications including acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, acute kidney injury, and delirium. She required ICU-level care for hypoxia and fluid overload, with initiation of IV diuresis and subsequent transition to hemodialysis due to worsening renal function and oliguria. A tunneled hemodialysis catheter was placed, and she was stabilized on dialysis three times weekly. Delirium, likely multifactorial from medications, surgery, and uremia, improved with medication adjustment and dialysis. A Pseudomonas urinary tract infection was treated with ciprofloxacin. Persistent knee pain was managed conservatively. She was discharged to extended care with plans for AV graft placement, ongoing dialysis, and outpatient follow-up with orthopedics and transplant surgery.

Initial scout image demonstrated the recently placed stent projected over the

Antegrade access into the graft was obtained by micropuncture technique and
placement of a 4.5 ___ microsheath.  Subsequent DSA runs demonstrated

After several attempts to back opacify the arterial anastomosis and arterial

established and a modified 4 ___ Glide catheter advanced up to the

The two microsheaths were removed, and a light pressure was held for about 5

1.  Patent AV graft with wall-to-wall flow and no evidence of thrombosis.
2.  Preserved central runoff without evidence of stenosis.  Notably, the
recently stented venous anastomosis of the graft appears unremarkable.
